overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of the resources AI depends on and who controls them. You'll be asked about the AI supply chain, energy and water use, concerns about market power, and export controls on advanced chips.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: Why have many AI model developers formed partnerships with cloud providers?

options.html: Competition law requires developers to share ownership with larger firms
options.text: Competition law requires developers to share ownership with larger firms
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. No such requirement exists. Developers form these partnerships because computing power is scarce and costs billions of dollars.

options.html: Computing power is scarce and costs billions of dollars
options.text: Computing power is scarce and costs billions of dollars
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Training and running large models takes more computing power than most developers can buy outright, and cloud providers own the data centers that supply it.

options.html: Cloud providers hold the patents on the methods used to train models
options.text: Cloud providers hold the patents on the methods used to train models
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The partnerships are about capacity, not patents. Developers form them because computing power is scarce and costs billions of dollars.

options.html: Developers are barred from buying the specialized chips for themselves
options.text: Developers are barred from buying the specialized chips for themselves
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Developers may buy chips, but supply is limited and the cost is very high. They form partnerships because computing power is scarce and costs billions of dollars.

forms.stemHtml: The International Energy Agency reports that data centers used about 415 terawatt-hours in 2024 and will use around 945 terawatt-hours by 2030. How do these two figures differ in kind?

options.html: The first covers all data centers and the second covers AI alone
options.text: The first covers all data centers and the second covers AI alone
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both cover data centers as a whole. The first is an estimate of present use, and the second is a projection.

options.html: The first is a company report and the second is a government count
options.text: The first is a company report and the second is a government count
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both come from the same agency. The first is an estimate of present use, and the second is a projection.

options.html: The first measures water and the second measures electricity
options.text: The first measures water and the second measures electricity
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both measure electricity. The first is an estimate of present use, and the second is a projection.

options.html: The first is an estimate and the second is a projection
options.text: The first is an estimate and the second is a projection
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The 2024 figure is built from data on what exists. The 2030 figure is calculated from assumptions about growth, and the agency's other scenarios give different results.

forms.stemHtml: Data centers used about 1.5 percent of the world's electricity in 2024. Why do many communities still treat them as a major issue?

options.html: Demand is concentrated, so local effects exceed the global share
options.text: Demand is concentrated, so local effects exceed the global share
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A single AI-focused data center can use as much electricity as 100,000 households, and a few countries and localities host most of the capacity.

options.html: The global figure leaves out every data center that is used to run AI
options.text: The global figure leaves out every data center that is used to run AI
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The figure includes AI data centers. Communities treat them as a major issue because demand is concentrated, so local effects exceed the global share.

options.html: Data centers use more electricity than all households combined
options.text: Data centers use more electricity than all households combined
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. At about 1.5 percent of world electricity, they don't. Demand is concentrated, so local effects exceed the global share.

options.html: The true global share is known to be many times higher
options.text: The true global share is known to be many times higher
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The figure is an estimate, and nothing shows it is many times too low. Demand is concentrated, so local effects exceed the global share.

forms.stemHtml: The UK's competition authority wrote that firms controlling critical inputs "may restrict access to them." What had the authority established when it wrote this?

options.html: That several firms had restricted access and broken the law
options.text: That several firms had restricted access and broken the law
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The authority made no finding of wrongdoing. It had established that a risk exists, and had not found that harm occurred.

options.html: That no firm in the sector holds any real market power
options.text: That no firm in the sector holds any real market power
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The authority was concerned about market power. It had established that a risk exists, and had not found that harm occurred.

options.html: That a risk exists, without finding that harm occurred
options.text: That a risk exists, without finding that harm occurred
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! "May" marks a possibility. The authority documented the partnerships and the limited supply of computing power, and warned of what could follow.

options.html: That partnerships in the sector always reduce competition
options.text: That partnerships in the sector always reduce competition
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The authority wrote that partnerships can bring benefits. It had established that a risk exists, and had not found that harm occurred.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements about United States export controls on advanced AI chips are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The policy toward China has changed several times since 2022
options.text: The policy toward China has changed several times since 2022
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Restrictions began in 2022, a tiered worldwide rule was issued and rescinded in 2025, and some sales to China were permitted under conditions from January 2026.

options.html: Supporters of restriction argue it slows a rival's progress in AI
options.text: Supporters of restriction argue it slows a rival's progress in AI
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is the security argument for denying a rival an input it can't easily make.

options.html: Supporters of controlled sales argue they keep a rival dependent on US technology
options.text: Supporters of controlled sales argue they keep a rival dependent on US technology
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! They also argue that sales fund US chip makers' future products.

options.html: Chip makers have no financial interest in which policy is chosen
options.text: Chip makers have no financial interest in which policy is chosen
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Chip makers gain directly from permission to sell, since China is a large market.

title: Chips, data centers, energy, and concentration of power
